pillars.note: No direct fire-safety pillar. The ACME CFI-G final report says only one of the six ACME experiments was focused on spacecraft fire safety, the Burning Rate Emulator (the word 'only' starts the first quoted line, split by the PDF text layer); E-FIELD Flames is another of the six. E-FIELD uses electric fields in microgravity combustion science (p. 3). Pillar list left empty on purpose; the reviewer should decide.

gravity_regime.note: The tests ran in microgravity on the ISS: the V-I curve behaves differently 'in microgravity as compared to 1-g flames' (p. 37) and the experiment is one of the ACME tests conducted in the CIR on the International Space Station (p. 3, the sentence wraps over two lines). The final report only suggests that electric fields 'may be a good tool for approximating buoyancy body forces at partial gravity' (p. 37), a finding and not a measured partial-gravity condition: no partial-gravity measurement exists. `partial_emulated` means emulation by electric field, never lunar or Martian gravity; the reviewer may prefer `microgravity`.
